header.name: Digital Communication Systems
header.description: This course will introduce students to the fundamental blocks that constitute a digital communication system. Starting with an introduction to source coding and characterization of communication signals and systems, the students will study the functionalities of the blocks such as Digital Modulator/ Digital Demodulator and Channel Encoder-Decoder. The performance of various digital modulation schemes along with the development of optimum receivers in the AWGN channel will be discussed. Further topics related to carrier synchronization and channel equalization shall be elaborated. Moreover, the course will also highlight the trade-off associated with bandwidth and power for linear block codes and digital modulation schemes.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Learn about data compression and review of information theory along with the review of signal space representation.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Study about probability of error and performance of QPSK, QAM, and DPSK and development of optimum receiver of signals with random phase AWGN channel.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Study on the importance of synchronization of signal demodulation, carrier freq and phase estimation, timing estimation-MMSE and ML methods, joint carrier, and symbol synchronization.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Equalization: Optical zero-forcing equalization, linear and decision feedback equalizers.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Error Correction: Linear Block Codes (LBC) and tradeoff between bandwidth and power for LBC and digital modulation schemes.

lecture_topics: Modulation techniques (M-ary PAM, M-ary PSK, DPSK, and M-ary QAM)
Probability of error of above modulation format with analysis in AWGN channel
development of optimum receiver under random phase
Carrier and Symbol Synchronization with lectures on importance of signal demodulation
Equalization: Zero Forcing and Linear equalizers with mention of decision feedback.
discussion on Modulation and Coding tradeoff
